maml:description.maml:para: Backs up the Vault using the CyberArk PAReplicate utility.

Runs PAReplicate.exe on the Replicate server to back up the Vault: a full backup by default, or an incremental backup with Incremental.
Equivalent to: PAReplicate \<VaultFile\> /LogonFromFile \<LogonFile\> \[/FullBackup\]
Back up as the built-in Backup user, enabled with a password set from the PrivateArk Client, or another user with the CABACKUP user type.
Only Safes that existed at the last full backup can be restored individually, so take a full backup regularly. Use Register-ARKBackupTask to schedule weekly incremental and full backups.
The name of the backup pool to back up to. Restores from this backup must use the same name.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.
The Vault user and password.
Runs an incremental backup. Without it, the backup is full, passed as /FullBackup.
The user credentials file, passed as /LogonFromFile.
A credentials file restricted to the SYSTEM OS user, for a scheduled task, cannot be used from an interactive session.
The Vault parameter file. Defaults to Vault.ini in the PAReplicate.exe folder.
Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet is not run.

maml:alert.maml:para:
Requires PAReplicate.exe, located with Set-ARKConfiguration -UtilityPath. PAReplicate.exe runs with its own folder as the working directory.
With Credential, the password is passed on the PAReplicate.exe command line and is visible to other processes on the machine while it runs. It is masked in debug output and error records. Use LogonFile to avoid this.
A non-zero exit code from PAReplicate.exe is reported as an error.

maml:introduction.maml:para: ``` Backup-ARKVault -LogonFile 'C:\Creds\backup.cred' ```
Runs a full backup, using Vault.ini in the PAReplicate folder.
``` Backup-ARKVault -LogonFile 'C:\Creds\backup.cred' -Incremental ```
Runs an incremental backup.
``` Backup-ARKVault -Credential (Get-Credential Backup) -BackupPoolName DRPool ```
Runs a full backup to the DRPool backup pool, logging on with a password.

maml:description.maml:para: Gets the default folders used by DRJones.

maml:introduction.maml:para: ``` Get-ARKConfiguration ```

maml:description.maml:para: Gets parameters from a CyberArk parameter file, such as DBParm.ini or Vault.ini.

maml:description.maml:para: Schedules weekly incremental and full Vault backups with the CyberArk PAReplicate utility.

Registers two scheduled tasks on the Replicate server that run PAReplicate.exe as SYSTEM, with its own folder as the working directory:
- PAReplicate Incremental Backup: PAReplicate \<VaultFile\> /LogonFromFile \<LogonFile\>, every day except FullBackupDay. - PAReplicate Full Backup: PAReplicate \<VaultFile\> /LogonFromFile \<LogonFile\> /FullBackup, on FullBackupDay.
Both tasks run at the same local time, and start as soon as possible after a missed start. Tasks with the same names in TaskPath are replaced.
Create the credentials file for the Backup user with CreateCredFile.exe, restricted to PAReplicate running as SYSTEM:
CreateCredFile.exe backup.cred Password /Username Backup /AppType CABACKUP /IpAddress /Hostname /ExePath "C:\Program Files (x86)\PrivateArk\Replicate\PAReplicate.exe" /OSUsername "NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM" /EntropyFile /DPAPIMachineProtection /Password \<password\>
The local time of day both backups start. Defaults to 01:00.
The name of the backup pool to back up to. Restores from these backups must use the same name.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.
The day of the week for the full backup. The incremental backup runs on every other day. Defaults to Sunday.
The user credentials file, passed as /LogonFromFile. Relative paths are resolved against the current location.
The Task Scheduler folder for the tasks, starting and ending with a backslash. Defaults to \DRJones\.
The Vault parameter file. Defaults to Vault.ini in the PAReplicate.exe folder.
Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet is not run.

maml:alert.maml:para:
Must run in an elevated session.
Requires PAReplicate.exe, located with Set-ARKConfiguration -UtilityPath.
The task results are recorded in the Task Scheduler history; PAReplicate.exe output is not captured.

maml:introduction.maml:para: ``` Register-ARKBackupTask -LogonFile 'C:\Program Files (x86)\PrivateArk\Replicate\backup.cred' ```
Schedules an incremental backup Monday to Saturday and a full backup on Sunday, at 01:00.
``` Register-ARKBackupTask -LogonFile 'C:\Program Files (x86)\PrivateArk\Replicate\backup.cred' -FullBackupDay Saturday -At '22:30' ```
Schedules the full backup on Saturday and the incremental backup on the other days, at 22:30.

maml:description.maml:para: Recovers restored full Vault backup files using CAVaultManager RecoverBackupFiles.

Runs CAVaultManager.exe RecoverBackupFiles to access the backup files in the Restored Safes folder with the Vault Recovery Private Key, and re-encrypt them with a new backup key, when the original backup key cannot be used.
Equivalent to: CAVaultManager RecoverBackupFiles /BackupPoolName \<BackupPoolName\>
The Recovery Private Key is read from the location set in the RecoveryPrvKey parameter of DBParm.ini.
Run after Restore-ARKVault with the Vault stopped, and before Restore-ARKVaultDatabase.
The name of the backup pool the backup files belong to.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.
Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet is not run.

maml:alert.maml:para:
Prompts for confirmation by default.
Requires the Recovery Private Key from the Master CD, set as RecoveryPrvKey in DBParm.ini. When the restore is complete, remove the Recovery Private Key from the Vault, and from any Safe or folder used to copy it there.
Must be run from an elevated session; the command throws otherwise.
Requires CAVaultManager.exe, located with Set-ARKConfiguration -UtilityPath. CAVaultManager.exe runs with its own folder as the working directory.
A non-zero exit code from CAVaultManager.exe is reported as an error.

maml:introduction.maml:para: ``` Repair-ARKVaultBackup ```
Recovers the backup files in the Restored Safes folder, after confirmation.
``` Repair-ARKVaultBackup -BackupPoolName PoolA -Confirm:$false ```
Recovers the backup files of the PoolA backup pool without prompting.

maml:description.maml:para: Decrypts Vault data files using the CyberArk Recover utility.

Runs Recover.exe to decrypt one or more encrypted Vault data files into an output folder, using the recovery keys in the key folder.
Equivalent to: Recover \<Path\> \<OutputPath\> \<KeyPath\> \[\<SafeRecoveryKeyPath\>\]
The output folder is created if it does not exist.
Relative paths are resolved against the current PowerShell location.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.
The folder containing the recovery keys. Defaults to the KeyPath set with Set-ARKConfiguration.
The folder to write the decrypted files to.
The encrypted data file to decrypt. Wildcards are passed to Recover.exe, which expands them.
The RSA-4096 Safe recovery key file, for Safes encrypted with a Safe recovery key.
Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet is not run.

maml:alert.maml:para:
Requires Recover.exe, located with Set-ARKConfiguration -UtilityPath. Recover.exe runs with its own folder as the working directory.
Recover.exe can run from any folder containing it and the DLLs, openssl.cnf and icudt74l.dat supplied with it in the Vault Server folder; these differ between Vault versions. Without openssl.cnf, Recover.exe fails with no output. The Visual C++ redistributable it requires must be installed. A missing DLL is reported as an error.
A non-zero exit code from Recover.exe is reported as an error.

maml:introduction.maml:para: ``` Restore-ARKFile -Path 'C:\Temp\my_data_file\*' -OutputPath 'D:\Restored' -KeyPath 'C:\Keys' ```
Decrypts all files in C:\Temp\my_data_file into D:\Restored using the recovery keys in C:\Keys.
``` Restore-ARKFile -Path 'C:\Temp\my_data_file\*' -OutputPath 'D:\Restored' -SafeRecoveryKeyPath 'C:\Temp\saferecover.key' ```
Decrypts the files using the default key folder set with Set-ARKConfiguration and an RSA-4096 Safe recovery key.
``` Get-ChildItem -Path 'C:\Temp\my_data_file' -File | Restore-ARKFile -OutputPath 'D:\Restored' ```
Decrypts each file found by Get-ChildItem, running Recover.exe once per file.

maml:description.maml:para: Restores a recordings Safe from backup into a new Safe using the CyberArk PARestore utility.

Runs PARestore.exe to restore a recordings Safe from the backup files into a new Safe in the Vault.
Equivalent to: PARestore \<VaultFile\> \<User\>/\<Password\> /RestoreRecordings /RestoreSafe \<Safe\> /TargetSafe \<TargetSafe\> /Owners \<Owners\> /Retention \<Retention\>
A Safe with the same name as the recordings Safe does not need to exist in the Vault. The target Safe must not exist; PARestore creates it, with the given owners and retention period.
The restoring user cannot be added as an owner of the restored Safe.
Recordings restored this way may not play in the PVWA (seen on v12.6 and v14.0). If they are needed, restore the whole Vault, with Restore-ARKVault, to an isolated server instead.
The name of the backup pool the backup files belong to. Must match the backup pool name used by PAReplicate.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.
The Vault user and password.
The user credentials file, passed as /LogonFromFile.
The users and groups to add as owners of the restored Safe. Defaults to Auditors.
The number of days, from 1 to 90, to keep the restored recordings. Defaults to 7.
The name of the recordings Safe to restore.
The name of the new Safe to restore into. The Safe must not already exist.
The Vault parameter file. Defaults to Vault.ini in the PARestore.exe folder.
Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet is not run.

maml:alert.maml:para:
Requires PARestore.exe, located with Set-ARKConfiguration -UtilityPath. PARestore.exe runs with its own folder as the working directory.
With Credential, the password is passed on the PARestore.exe command line and is visible to other processes on the machine while it runs. It is masked in debug output and error records. Use LogonFile to avoid this.
PARestore.exe runs in the current console, so its prompts, such as the warning about the supported PVWA version, are shown and answered there. Its output is not captured: StdOut and StdErr of the result are empty. Run the command from a console host, such as pwsh or the VS Code terminal.
A non-zero exit code from PARestore.exe is reported as an error.
PARestore.exe locks Vault database tables while it runs, so it can take a long time and Vault logons can fail or time out until it finishes. Run it when Vault activity is low.

maml:introduction.maml:para: ``` Restore-ARKRecordingSafe -Safe PSMRecordings -TargetSafe PSMRecordings_R -Credential (Get-Credential Backup) ```
Restores the PSMRecordings Safe into a new Safe named PSMRecordings_R, owned by Auditors with a 7 day retention.
``` Restore-ARKRecordingSafe PSMRecordings PSMRecordings_R -Owners Auditors, 'Vault Admins' -Retention 30 -Credential $Cred ```
Restores the recordings Safe with Auditors and Vault Admins as owners, keeping recordings for 30 days.

maml:description.maml:para: Decrypts the contents of a Vault Safe using the CyberArk SafeRecover utility.

Runs SafeRecover.exe to decrypt the contents of one or more Safes into an output folder, using the master key in the key folder. SafeRecover.exe reads the Safe data from the SafesDirectory set in tsparm.ini on the Vault server.
Equivalent to: SafeRecover \<Safe\> \<OutputPath\> \<KeyPath\>
The output folder is created if it does not exist.
Relative paths are resolved against the current PowerShell location.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.
The folder containing the master key. Defaults to the KeyPath set with Set-ARKConfiguration.
The folder to write the decrypted Safe contents to.
The name of the Safe to decrypt. Wildcards are passed to SafeRecover.exe, which expands them.
Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet is not run.

maml:alert.maml:para:
Must be run from an elevated session; the command throws otherwise.
Requires SafeRecover.exe, located with Set-ARKConfiguration -UtilityPath. SafeRecover.exe runs with its own folder as the working directory.
SafeRecover.exe reads the Vault Server registry settings, so it must run on a Vault server; elsewhere it fails with ITASE001S System error: RegOpenKey_1 failed. The PrivateArk Server service must be stopped; the command throws if it is running. The PrivateArk Database service must be running.

maml:introduction.maml:para: ``` Restore-ARKSafe -Safe Research -OutputPath 'C:\Research' -KeyPath 'C:\MasterKey' ```

``` Restore-ARKSafe -Safe 'Fin*' -OutputPath 'D:\Restored' ```

``` Import-Csv -Path .\Safes.csv | Restore-ARKSafe ```
Decrypts each Safe listed in a CSV file with SafeName and OutputPath columns.

maml:description.maml:para: Copies full Vault backup files to the Vault using the CyberArk PARestore utility.

Runs PARestore.exe to copy the backup files of the entire Vault to the Restored Safes folder on the Vault server, as the first step of a full Vault restore.
Equivalent to: PARestore \<VaultFile\> \<User\>/\<Password\> /FullVaultRestore
All data in the destination Vault is overwritten. The destination Vault must have been installed with the same keys as the Vault that was backed up.
The full Vault restore procedure is:
1. Start the destination Vault, with no PADR services running, and enable a user with the Restore All Safes authorization, such as Operator. 2. On the destination Vault, Set-ARKVaultParameter in DBParm.ini: BackupFilesDeletion=No, and RecoveryPrvKey pointing to the Recovery Private Key on the Master CD. 3. On the Replicate server, Set-ARKVaultParameter in Vault.ini: ADDRESS of the destination Vault. 4. On the Replicate server, Restore-ARKVault to copy the backup files, with -FromRestored if an archived copy of the backup files was restored to the local Restored Safes folder. 5. Stop the destination Vault. 6. On the destination Vault, Repair-ARKVaultBackup to recover the backup files. 7. Restore-ARKVaultDatabase. 8. Reset BackupFilesDeletion in DBParm.ini (default Yes,24,1,5,7d), and remove the Recovery Private Key from the Vault. 9. Start the Vault.
The name of the backup pool the backup files belong to. Must match the backup pool name used by PAReplicate.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.
The Vault user and password.

Copies the backup files from the Restored Safes folder on this machine, next to the SafesDirectory set in tsparm.ini, instead of from the Safes folder. Use it when an archived copy of the PAReplicate backup files has been restored there. Passed as /FromRestored.
The user credentials file, passed as /LogonFromFile.
The Vault parameter file. Defaults to Vault.ini in the PARestore.exe folder.
Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet is not run.

maml:alert.maml:para:
Prompts for confirmation by default.
Must be run from an elevated session; the command throws otherwise.
The upload can take a long time, and the PARestore.exe output is returned only when it completes. Monitor the size of the Restored Safes folder on the destination Vault to follow progress.
Requires PARestore.exe, located with Set-ARKConfiguration -UtilityPath. PARestore.exe runs with its own folder as the working directory.
With Credential, the password is passed on the PARestore.exe command line and is visible to other processes on the machine while it runs. It is masked in debug output and error records. Use LogonFile to avoid this.
A non-zero exit code from PARestore.exe is reported as an error.

maml:introduction.maml:para: ``` Restore-ARKVault -Credential (Get-Credential Operator) ```
Copies the full Vault backup files to the Restored Safes folder, using Vault.ini in the PARestore folder.
``` Restore-ARKVault -LogonFile 'C:\Creds\Operator.cred' -FromRestored -Confirm:$false ```
Logs on with a credentials file and copies the archived backup files restored to the local Restored Safes folder, without prompting.

maml:description.maml:para: Restores the Vault database from the Restored Safes folder using CAVaultManager RestoreDB.

Equivalent to: CAVaultManager RestoreDB /BackupPoolName \<BackupPoolName\> /NoSynchronize /Force
After the database is restored, CAVaultManager synchronizes it with the restored Safe files unless NoSynchronize is specified.
The Vault must be stopped, and the session must be elevated.
The name of the backup pool the backup files belong to.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.
Skips synchronizing the restored database with the restored Safe files. Use Sync-ARKVaultDatabase to synchronize later.
Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet is not run.

maml:alert.maml:para:
Prompts for confirmation by default; CAVaultManager.exe is always run with /Force so it does not prompt.
Must be run from an elevated session; the command throws otherwise.
Requires CAVaultManager.exe, located with Set-ARKConfiguration -UtilityPath. CAVaultManager.exe runs with its own folder as the working directory.
A non-zero exit code from CAVaultManager.exe is reported as an error.

maml:introduction.maml:para: ``` Restore-ARKVaultDatabase ```
Restores the Vault database and synchronizes it with the restored Safe files, after confirmation.
``` Restore-ARKVaultDatabase -BackupPoolName PoolA -NoSynchronize -Confirm:$false ```
Restores the Vault database from the PoolA backup pool without synchronizing, without prompting.

maml:description.maml:para: Restores a Safe from backup into a new Safe using the CyberArk PARestore utility.

Runs PARestore.exe to restore a single Safe from the backup files into a new Safe in the Vault.
Equivalent to: PARestore \<VaultFile\> \<User\>/\<Password\> /RestoreSafe \<Safe\> /TargetSafe \<TargetSafe\>
A Safe with the same name as the Safe being restored must exist in the Vault. If the original Safe was deleted, create an empty Safe with the same name, with the same owners as the original. The target Safe must not exist; PARestore creates it, with the owners of the Safe with the same name. Backed-up owners that are not owners of that Safe are removed from the target Safe and reported as ITATS658W warnings; if every owner is removed, only the Master user can access the target Safe.
The restoring user needs the Restore All Safes Vault authorization, typically the Operator user, or the Backup Safe authorization in the Safe being restored. It must be an owner of the Safe with the same name, but cannot be an owner of the restored Safe, so Administrator cannot be used. A user created to run PARestore must have the CABACKUP user type, which needs a CABACKUP license.
Only Safes that existed at the last full backup can be restored. A Safe created since then, held only in incremental backups, cannot be restored individually: restore the full Vault to an isolated server, take a full backup there, and restore the Safe from that backup.
To restore from an older backup, point SafesDirectory in tsparm.ini in the PARestore.exe folder at a folder holding the complete Metadata folder and the Data folder of each Safe to restore, all from the same backup. Revert tsparm.ini before the next PAReplicate backup runs.
Dependencies of restored accounts (Windows Server, Scheduled Task, IIS Application, Windows Registry, COM+ Application, IIS Anonymous User) are not linked to their accounts and show as empty lines in the PVWA. Add them again from the PVWA, then remove the original dependency files from the Safe with the PrivateArk Client.
The name of the backup pool the backup files belong to. Must match the backup pool name used by PAReplicate.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.
The Vault user and password.

Restores only the Safe data files, into a new target Safe. The Vault metadata must already have been restored by an earlier restore from the same backup, for example of another Safe. A DataOnly restore into the target Safe of a MetadataOnly restore fails with ITATS654E. Cannot be used with MetadataOnly.

Restores the Safe to the Vault from the files already in the Restored Safes folder on the Vault server. Use after copying the complete Metadata folder and the Data folder of the Safe there, from a third-party backup or an older PAReplicate backup.
The user credentials file, passed as /LogonFromFile.
Restores only the Safe metadata, without the data files. The restored files are reported missing (ITATS850W) and their records kept in the Safe. Cannot be used with DataOnly.
The name of the Safe to restore.
The name of the new Safe to restore into. The Safe must not already exist.
The Vault parameter file. Defaults to Vault.ini in the PARestore.exe folder.
Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet is not run.

maml:alert.maml:para:
Requires PARestore.exe, located with Set-ARKConfiguration -UtilityPath. PARestore.exe runs with its own folder as the working directory.
With Credential, the password is passed on the PARestore.exe command line and is visible to other processes on the machine while it runs. It is masked in debug output and error records. Use LogonFile to avoid this.
A non-zero exit code from PARestore.exe is reported as an error. Each ITATS658W line in the PARestore.exe output is also written as a warning.
PARestore.exe locks Vault database tables while it runs, so it can take a long time and Vault logons can fail or time out until it finishes. Run it when Vault activity is low.

maml:introduction.maml:para: ``` Restore-ARKVaultSafe -Safe Banners -TargetSafe Banners_R -Credential (Get-Credential Backup) ```
Restores the Banners Safe into a new Safe named Banners_R, using Vault.ini in the PARestore folder.
``` Restore-ARKVaultSafe Banners Banners_R -LogonFile 'C:\Creds\Backup.cred' -VaultFile 'C:\PrivateArk\Server\Vault.ini' ```
Restores the Banners Safe, logging on with a credentials file and a specific Vault parameter file.
``` Restore-ARKVaultSafe -Safe Vines -TargetSafe Vines_R -Credential $Cred -DataOnly ```
Restores only the data files of the Vines Safe, after an earlier restore from the same backup restored the metadata.
``` Restore-ARKVaultSafe -Safe Banners -TargetSafe Banners_R -LogonFile 'C:\Creds\Operator.cred' -LoadOnly ```

Restores a Safe from files copied manually, for example from a third-party backup: copy the complete Metadata folder and the Data folder of the Safe, unrenamed, into the Restored Safes folder on the Vault server first.

maml:description.maml:para: Sets the default folders used by DRJones.

Sets the folders containing the CyberArk recovery utilities (Recover.exe, SafeRecover.exe, PARestore.exe and CAVaultManager.exe), and the default folder containing the recovery keys.
When several utility folders are set, each utility is run from the first folder that contains it.
The configuration is saved to DRJonesConfiguration.xml in the user's home folder and loaded when the module is imported.
Only the values provided are changed; any existing value of a parameter not provided is kept.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.
The default folder containing the recovery keys, used when -KeyPath is not provided to Restore-ARKFile or Restore-ARKSafe.
The folders containing the recovery utilities, searched in order.
Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet is not run.

maml:introduction.maml:para: ``` Set-ARKConfiguration -UtilityPath 'C:\Program Files (x86)\PrivateArk\Server' -KeyPath 'D:\RecoveryKeys' ```
Sets the utility folder and the default recovery key folder.
``` Set-ARKConfiguration -KeyPath 'E:\MasterKey' ```
Changes the default recovery key folder, keeping the configured utility folder.
``` Set-ARKConfiguration -UtilityPath 'C:\Program Files (x86)\PrivateArk\Replicate', 'C:\Program Files (x86)\PrivateArk\Server' ```
Sets the Replicate folder (PARestore.exe) and the Vault Server folder (CAVaultManager.exe) as utility folders.

maml:description.maml:para: Sets a parameter in a CyberArk parameter file, such as DBParm.ini or Vault.ini.

Changes the value of a parameter in a CyberArk parameter file, keeping the rest of the file unchanged.
If the parameter already exists, its value is changed wherever it is in the file. If it does not exist, it is added to the end of the section given in Section, creating the section if needed. In a file without sections, a new parameter is added to the end of the file.
Use to prepare the Vault for a full Vault restore, and to reset it afterwards.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.
The parameter name.
The parameter file.
The section to add the parameter to, if it is not already in the file. Required to add a parameter to a file with sections.
The parameter value, written as given.
Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet is not run.

maml:alert.maml:para:
The file keeps its encoding; lines are written with CRLF line endings.
The Vault reads DBParm.ini when it starts; restart the Vault for changes to take effect.

maml:introduction.maml:para: ``` $DBParm = 'C:\Program Files (x86)\PrivateArk\Server\Conf\DBParm.ini' Set-ARKVaultParameter -Path $DBParm -Name BackupFilesDeletion -Value No -Section BACKUP Set-ARKVaultParameter -Path $DBParm -Name RecoveryPrvKey -Value 'D:\recprv.key' -Section MAIN ```
Prepares DBParm.ini for a full Vault restore: keeps the restored backup files, and points to the Recovery Private Key on the Master CD.
``` Set-ARKVaultParameter -Path $DBParm -Name BackupFilesDeletion -Value 'Yes,24,1,5,7d' ```
Resets BackupFilesDeletion to its default after a full Vault restore.
``` Set-ARKVaultParameter -Path 'C:\Program Files (x86)\PrivateArk\Replicate\Vault.ini' -Name ADDRESS -Value 10.0.0.5 ```
Points PARestore.exe at the destination Vault.

maml:description.maml:para: Synchronizes the Vault database with the restored Safe files using CAVaultManager SynchronizeDB.

Runs CAVaultManager.exe SynchronizeDB to synchronize the restored Vault metadata with the files and quotas in the Safes folder, for example after Restore-ARKVaultDatabase -NoSynchronize.
Equivalent to: CAVaultManager SynchronizeDB /SafePattern \<SafePattern\> /FilesSyncOnly /QuotaSyncOnly /Update /Force
Without Update, the synchronization is only simulated and the differences are reported in the output. With Update, the database is changed, after confirmation.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet with Update.
Synchronizes only the files in the Safes folder with the restored metadata.
Synchronizes only the quotas in the Safes folder with the restored metadata.
The Safes to synchronize, as a name or wildcard pattern. Defaults to all Safes.
Updates the database. Without Update, the synchronization is only simulated.
Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs with Update. The cmdlet is not run.

maml:alert.maml:para:
With Update, prompts for confirmation by default; CAVaultManager.exe is always run with /Force so it does not prompt.
Requires CAVaultManager.exe, located with Set-ARKConfiguration -UtilityPath. CAVaultManager.exe runs with its own folder as the working directory.

maml:introduction.maml:para: ``` Sync-ARKVaultDatabase ```
Simulates synchronizing all Safes, reporting the differences without changing the database.
``` Sync-ARKVaultDatabase -SafePattern 'Fin*' -FilesSyncOnly -Update ```
Synchronizes the files of Safes with names starting Fin with the restored metadata, after confirmation.
